answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

Scope and data volume
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the March 2016 time span).
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849, of which 34 are above the catalogue magnitude of completeness Mc.
- Pumping over 15.96 days: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 (net extraction).
- Catalogue (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016): 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07.

CALIBRATED result (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5; magnitudes from the LBNL catalogue, so this is the calibrated probability):
- b = 1.0: Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922, P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474, P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection is counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
- b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated (LBNL catalogue) probabilities indicate a very low likelihood of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 earthquake per year at Brady Hot Springs during March 2016 (0.00012-0.0147 per year depending on b), while the DAS-based number (0.07842/yr) is an upper bound only, because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all detections are treated as events >= Mc, inflating the count.
